notes: No argument, and a type token that is not an abbreviation of mob/obj, both emit the usage line — which has NO terminator.
is_abbrev(buf, "mob") accepts "m"/"mo"/"mob" and rejects the longer "mobs" (the token must be a prefix of the table word), so "mobs" takes the usage path while "m" resolves to the mob branch.
An omitted field token makes old_search_block return 0 for the empty argument, which is the only way to reach "No field by that name. Try 'help string'.".
A non-empty unknown field makes old_search_block return -1, so control reaches the switch default instead: "That field is undefined for monsters/objects.".
get_char_vis failure emits "I don't know anyone by that name..." and a carried-object miss emits "Nothing by that name.." — two dots, on purpose.
name/short/long/description write the live NPC fields and acknowledge with "Ok.\n\r"; the room look after the edit proves the instance, not the prototype, changed.
short and long are monsters-only for a player target; title on an NPC emits "Monsters have no titles.".
length[] = {15,60,256,240,60}; the inline notice is "String too long - truncated.\n\r" — lower-case t, LFCR, unlike string_add's own notice.
C appends a real CRLF inside the field-3 case before the inline/editor test, so `string mob x long` writes "\r\n" and reports Ok instead of opening the editor.
name/short/long write the live carried object (Runtime overrides); the inventory line proves the new short description.
Field 5 (title) and any rejected value fall to "That field is undefined for objects.".
A new keyword creates the node at the head of the live ex_description list ("New field.\n\r") and the following look <keyword> resolves it.
str_cmp (utils.c:107) is a case-insensitive exact compare, so a differently-cased keyword modifies the same node instead of adding one.
Head-node delete frees the node and emits "Field deleted.\n\r"; the following look <keyword> misses.
do_string never calls string_write, so d->str points at the live field: every accepted line is visible immediately (proved by /l and by the room look before the editor closes).
STATE(d) is CON_PLAYING, which the abort switch does not handle, so /a logs "SYSERR: string_add: Aborting write from unknown origin." and restores nothing — the written-through text stays.
/c frees the buffer and writes the empty field through; the next line therefore takes string_add's first-line branch again.
A player target refuses short/long with "That field is for monsters only.\n\r" regardless of the actor's level.

While d->str is set make_prompt returns a bare "] " — keyed on the descriptor string pointer, not PLR_WRITING, which do_string never sets because it bypasses string_write. The same CON_PLAYING flush also carries process_output's extra CRLF before the prompt, giving the blank line the oracle shows after "New field." Found by this vehicle; fixed in session_send.go.

Transport line-ending class this command exposed: a handler message ending in C's LFCR pair ("\n\r") had a second CRLF appended by the telnet writer, inserting a blank line between the WARNING and Ok messages of a single command. pkg/telnet now treats any trailing '\n' or '\r' as terminated.

FORCED DIVERGENCE. find_exdesc walks the whole list but the guard at :722 compares only the head, so deleting a non-head field falls through to the standard tail with field==6: length[5] is read past the 5-element array and CREATE() writes through the NULL d->str do_string never set — a segfault. The port emits nothing, keeps the list, and logs the SYSERR shape; excluded from the oracle vehicle because the C side would crash instead of producing a transcript.
find_exdesc returns the matching entry's description pointer, so a field created by field 4 but never written reads as "No field with that keyword." even though the keyword exists.
string_add's own notices differ from the inline ones in both case and terminator: "String too long - Truncated.\r\n" (first line) and "String too long.  Last line skipped.\r\n" (two spaces).
`*ch->desc->str = 0` runs before the first editor line, so the previous text is already gone on entry and cannot come back.
playing_string_cleanup only has PLR_MAILING and board branches, so both save exits (@ and /s) print nothing and emit no room act.
close_socket drops the descriptor without a string cleanup for CON_PLAYING: the written-through text survives and no abort notice is printed.
get_obj() has zero callers anywhere in src/ and is not on do_string's call path (get_char_vis at :620, get_obj_in_list_vis at :668). Do not port it — R4/R5e.

`if (IS_NPC(ch)) return;` is a silent return. A switched immortal is refused earlier by the immortal-command gate (commands.go commandGateRejected, MinLevel 32 >= LVL_IMMORT), so the branch has no reachable case in the port.
Per-field gate inside the command: below LEVEL_IMPL-1 the refusal ("You can't change that field for players.", no terminator); at LEVEL_IMPL-1 the WARNING line precedes the standard tail.
